data.content_ref: inline:The contradiction rests on an asserted causal claim — that forced mechanism-sharing connections 'destroy the very signal that isolation provides' — with no causal mechanism identified. From the demand-a-causal-mechanism stance, the target must show HOW a forced connection in one part of the artifact graph causally undermines the diagnostic value of isolation elsewhere. Instead it simply posits epistemic incompatibility as self-evident. The refutation condition itself concedes the two might coexist, undermining the claim that this is a genuine contradiction rather than a tentative disagreement about epistemic values.
